utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we resume in the examination of the witness, I would like to raise a few issues just very shortly. The first one is that the Chamber gets the impression that some witnesses are called for the Prosecution at this very moment who do not appear on the revised list we received before. This, of course, comes as a surprise and, for example, the witness Eterovic does not appear on that list. So if the Chamber could be informed about what this list still means, it would be highly appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could very briefly. My understanding is that Mr. Ierace sent a letter to the Defence counsel, with a copy to the Chamber, indicating that there were three witnesses on the list that was handed up several weeks ago whose names were unintentionally omitted. I also understand from a discussion I had this morning with Mr. Ierace that he is in the process of refining the list to also include dropping a couple of witnesses who were on the revised list that was handed up. Perhaps at the conclusion of the current witness or shortly before the first break, Mr. Ierace could be made available to further enlighten the Chamber in that respect if that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we might have overlooked part of the very frequent correspondence between the parties, so we'll first check that. I don't think it is very urgent at this very moment but, of course, we would like to be informed about --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. As I indicated, Mr. Ierace is in the process of developing a more refined witness list to include -- excluding several other witnesses who were on the revised list that was handed up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we will be informed about it. The second issue is that we received quite some time ago already some 92 bis statements, especially statements about the authenticity of medical records, et cetera. Since it was not that consistent, especially the statements attached to it and whether it was repetitious or not -- well, we asked to revise it and we never saw it again. I don't know whether that is the intention to, but I think the procedure was that they had to be filed in a final version and a request should have been made to the Chamber to have admit them into evidence so that we can give a decision on that and, of course, we have already observations that were made by the Defence. So we expect some information or some new developments in that respect or an indication that, for whatever reason, the Prosecution is not wishing to pursue these 92 bis -- the admission of these 92 bis statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, I will ensure that Mr. Ierace is prepared to address that later this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the last issue I would like to raise, and I don't think we have to go into closed session, is about Witness AD. The Chamber, without expressing itself on the basis of the objections, and the basis of the objection was that the rights of the Defence had been violated, but apart from that, if the Defence would like to make submissions in that respect commenting on the request of the Prosecutor, we will receive them, we will pay proper attention to it and we will see whether it causes us to reconsider the decision the Chamber gave yesterday. The Chamber thinks that one week would be an appropriate time limit to prepare these submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you very much for your remark. I informed Madam Registrar earlier of the fact that a request to file an appeal is already before your Chamber since this morning, and considering there was a violation of essentially no one is guaranteeing the rights of the accused to a fair trial, we formulated an appeal according to the Rule 73(B) and we filed a request with your Chamber to make sure that the interrogatory appeal was possible on this subject. It seems to me that otherwise it would have maybe been misunderstood. That is why we filed it immediately. We could have done it within seven days, but we did it immediately, Mr. President - it was either early this morning or a little later - with the objective of gaining time, considering that on the 5th of July, the Prosecution should finish its case. So we did not use the notice, the seven-day notice that we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just since 10 seconds the Defence response and Prosecution motion in my hands, and it is highly appreciated that it has been done in such a quick way. Thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there are two matters on one hand. There is forms that was filed yesterday directly and then, on the other hand, parallel with that, there is a request to authorise an appeal which is somewhere in the Tribunal administration which was filed -- which was given this morning to the Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will -- I have not seen yet that application for an authorisation to have an interlocutory appeal against the decision but at least we received by now your response on the request as it has been made by the Prosecution. These were the issues I would like to raise at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am informed, do I understand you well, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that the application for authorisation to appeal -- an interlocutory appeal was filed with the Registry, not with our registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... perhaps perfectly in the transcript, but perhaps that is clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday, the Prosecution concluded the examination-in-chief of the Witness Husovic. Is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness? I noted that the examination-in-chief took 25 minutes. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Husovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How are you doing, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will now be examined by counsel for the Defence. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Husovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, can you confirm that on the 3rd of March, 1995, you made a statement to the security centre in Sarajevo about the incident you testified about yesterday during the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 23rd of February, 1996, did you make a statement to investigators of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, yesterday, during your examination-in-chief, you said that you had been shot at from the direction of Hrasno Brdo?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you that in the statement you made to the Public Security centre in Novo Sarajevo on the 3rd of March, 1995, which is Prosecution Exhibit -- you stated in line 4, "Shot from the direction of the Grbavica settlement." You were speaking of the event of the 10th of January, 1994, and you said that you had been shot at from the direction of the neighbourhood of Grbavica. Would you tell us, please, which statement is correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The correct statement would be that I was shot at from the location of Hrasno hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why you stated on the 3rd of March, 1995, that you had been shot at from the direction of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I was talking to Mr. Barry Hogan and when I look at the map, then I realised that there is no way the bullet could come from that area, that it would be from Hrasno hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not sure even now from which direction you were shot at on the 10th of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may be permitted to interrupt. The document Defence counsel is referring to is not this witness's statement. It is a police report. I presume you are referring to Exhibit number 2114?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look because Ms. Pilipovic has mentioned the number of the exhibit -- the number of the document and it is not in my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us, please, Ms. Pilipovic, because you started saying, "which is Prosecution Exhibit" and then the transcript remains silent on the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have before me an official note, a report of the centre, and it is numbered 2114. I think that yesterday the statement made by Mr. Husovic was tendered into evidence. If not, the Defence has a sufficient number of copies in the native language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is no problem as such, but you referred, without giving the number, to a statement of the witness and the Prosecution objects against this qualification of the document because the Prosecution says it is not a statement of the witness, but it is a report, which --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has Prosecution document ERN number 00306755. We have a sufficient number of copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is a statement of this witness, yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is a statement. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As you know, if it is just a small part, you can read it. If it is a small document and the document as a whole is relevant, you, of course, can show it to the witness and to the Bench and to the Prosecution. Ms. Mahindaratne, I do understand now that the Defence is going to -- is going to present to the witness document not being 2114 but another document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would the usher please, if necessary, show the document to the witness so that he can identify it and tell us whether it is his statement or not. And I will just read.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, is this the statement that you made in the Public Security Centre on the 3rd of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. But I do realise after I spoke with Mr. Barry Hogan--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that you want to add something but perhaps the first question was whether you recognise this document as the statement you gave to the -- to the security --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, in line 4 of your statement does it say: "Shot from the direction of the Grbavica neighbourhood"? Did you say that and is that what the document says? Is it the way you said it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. But I think when I spoke with this gentleman, Mr. Barry Hogan, I realised that bullet could not come from that place because it was too far from that location. And even though if -- if you are referring to this also, this was controlled by Serb forces, by army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "this was controlled by the army of Republika Srpska," what part of town are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is like east, south-east side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us the name of that area?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, when talking to the OTP investigator, you were not sure from which direction you had been shot at?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that even today you do not know the direction from which the shot came?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know, and I was shot from Hrasno hill.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, yesterday, during the examination-in-chief in chief, in response to my learned friend's question, you said that on the occasion of the incident that happened on the 12th of January -- on the 10th of January, an official report had been drawn up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the official report was drawn up, were you interviewed about the incident?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You confirm then that you talked to the person who drew up the official report, Samir Selimovic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the interview with Mr. Selimovic took place?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in the hospital because it has been like six years. I am not really sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, if I put it to you or, rather, if I show you the official report, P2114, in which it says: "Before the Paradiso building," this is the first line of the second part, "in front of the Paradiso establishment where Edin Husovic was wounded, most probably by a stray bullet from the direction of the aggressor positions in Grbavica," would that be correct? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be direct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you confirm then that on the 12th of January, 1994, after the incident took place, a stray bullet was mentioned coming from the direction of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I may be permitted to interrupt, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It is unfair to place these questions without showing him the statement he has made to the investigator who prepared the report. The investigator's report uses the words "stray bullet" but nowhere in the statement does it talk about a stray bullet. The questions are based on the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Official report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We usually confront the witness with the literal wording of a certain text. If not, the whole text is relevant, and therefore, Ms. Pilipovic, would you please read out specifically and indicate clearly whether it is a report or not. It is not clearly in my mind at this moment. Yes, you said it was from the official report, that is 2114, and Ms. Pilipovic has confronted the witness with the text in this report. So it must be clear to the witness that the part read was part of a report and not of his own statement. On the other hand, it might be a bit confusing, Ms. Pilipovic, that you then asked the witness: "Did you say that?" That might create confusion on whether it is a statement or a report. But if you would have asked the witness whether he gave such information to those who drafted the report, then of course it would be perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I asked the witness whether he had been interviewed by the person who made up the report on the 12th of January, 1994, and the witness said he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, while being interviewed by Mr. Samir Semilovic, who drew up the report, did you tell the investigator about the event that took place, and was this on the 12th of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on 10th of January, 1994, and I never did say that it was a stray bullet. I was referring to sniper shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you on that occasion tell Mr. Selimovic that the stray bullet was fired from the direction of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that it was a stray bullet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, in you question, you more or less ignored what the witness said. So if you would have asked whether he told Mr. Selimovic that the bullet was fired from the direction of Grbavica, that would be fair.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the direction of Grbavica. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell Mr. Selimovic that the bullet was fired from the direction of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you talked to the investigator of the Prosecutor's office about the incident, about what happened to you, did you say that the shot was fired from Hrasno Brdo, and in 1994, that is on the 10th of January, did you know what army was holding the positions on Hrasno Brdo?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know, and it was army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you that the front lines on Hrasno Brdo were 50 metres apart and that they were separated by streets and that Hrasno Brdo was divided up, would you agree with me that that was correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not really sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, you said yesterday that you were standing in front of the Paradiso restaurant with your friends and that this was in Cengic Vila; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your friends were wearing civilian uniforms?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that Mr. Mirsad Abdurahmanovic and Mr. Kahriman were members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the clothes they were wearing which you say was civilian, were they wearing any insignia indicating that they were members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you that your friend Mirsad Abdurahmanovic was a member of the army from 1992 and that he belonged to the 102nd Motorised Brigade, would you agree with me that that was correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not really sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you that he told the Prosecution investigator, Mr. Barry Hogan, on the 24th of September, 2001, that he had joined the army in 1992 and that he was a member of the 102nd Motorised Brigade, and that the headquarters of that brigade was in the Zica company, would you agree with me that that was correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not really sure if he joined the army or not, but while he was standing with us, he was in civilian clothes and he was not a soldier. I am sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are telling us that Mr. Mirsad Abdurahmanovic's statement and his interview, what he said to the investigator, that he was a member of the 102nd Motorised Brigade, is not correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whatever he said or not, but I am not really sure whether he was in the army or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When as you say you were wounded on the 10th of January, you said that Mr. Abdurahmanovic took you to hospital. Is that correct or am I wrong? Tell us who took you to hospital.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sead Kahriman, he took me to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what vehicle he used to take you to hospital?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a Golf, Volkswagen Golf. It was red colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period 1992, 1993, 1994, did you know that Golf cars were used to carry mortars around the part of Sarajevo that was under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, you told us that in 1994 you were 17 and that you went to school. Can you tell us what school you attended? What was the name of your school?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Saobracajna, just like -- I really cannot translate this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Transport school or traffic school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Traffic school.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in the part of town where you lived, schools and kindergartens were used to accommodate soldiers of the 102nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not really sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the part of town you lived in, you say this was the Cengic Vila neighbourhood. Was there a kindergarten called the 8th of March, Osmi Mart at the time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not really sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Otoka neighbourhood, was there also a kindergarten?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was. I am not really sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you that in the 8th of March kindergarten in Cengic Vila and in the kindergarten in Otoka, the 102nd Motorised Brigade in 1993 and 1994 accommodated soldiers, would you agree with me that that was correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not really sure. So.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you something, Mr. Husovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You repeatedly gave us an answer, "I am not really sure." That suggests that you have some information you might not be sure about --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Like I said, I was student at the time so maybe if there was such an army in those kindergartens, I wouldn't have access and I wouldn't -- I couldn't give a correct information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that, but let's just, by way of example --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you never had access to a school where you nevertheless had some information that there might have been military accommodation, for example, you saw military people going there on a regular basis. I have some difficulty in understanding what you mean by, "I am not really sure." That means that you are not saying you don't really know about it. You are not saying that you never heard about it. You say, "I am not really sure." That is several times you did it. So you might have had some clue. If you have any clue, even if you are not sure, tell us about the clue you had. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, in 1994, you were 17. Did your peers or, rather, were other young men your age members of the army? Did you have any friends who joined the army who were the same age as you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe they did and I really don't know about it. None of my friends did, so...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interfere again. You told us before that you did not know whether Mr. Abdurahmanovic joined the army or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment you say: "I don't know. Maybe they did." You don't know about whether they joined the army. I don't know whether Mr. Abdurahmanovic is approximately your age.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is older than me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are concentrating your answer on the age, but would he be 18, 19, 20 or 25?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mirsad, I knew him but not that well, so he was not like really close friend with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But are you sure that he did not join the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know I would see him around the neighbourhood and he was always in civilian clothes. I didn't know if he was in the army or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But your testimony was that none of your friends did join the army. Now you say, "I am not sure." Well, to repeat my earlier words, "I have no clue to assume that he joined the army." Is that what you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, near your neighbourhood, the neighbourhood where you lived, was there a company called Vranica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you that a witness who testified before this court, Mr. Mirsad Sabljica, said that the headquarters of the 102nd Motorised Brigade was in the Vranica company, would you agree with me that that was correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree because I don't know. I am not really sure. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, 1993, and 1994, did you see soldiers of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what they were wearing, I mean the members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? I am referring specifically to the year 1994.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you used to see soldiers in camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the city, so I would see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers in the part of town called Cengic Vila and Dolac Malta?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers in those two neighbourhoods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether these soldiers gathered in a certain place in these two neighbourhoods?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know really, so...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you would see them in uniform, does that mean they were walking around in the part of town where you saw them?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were walking around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see soldiers in the Paradiso Cafe in uniform, in army of Bosnia-Herzegovina uniform? I don't mean on that day because you said you didn't on that day, but did they frequent the cafe?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not. There were no soldiers in that cafe, ever. It was only civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see your friend Mirsad Abdurahmanovic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really say. Maybe every 10 days. Every two days, a few days. Every few days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, 1993, 1994, did you see him at 2 to 10 day intervals and was he in uniform when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said, I don't know he was a soldier and I never saw him in uniform before. He was always wearing civilian clothes and so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you went to school. In 1992, 1993, 1994, were you going to school then?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the part of town are you lived, was there a building belonging to the Energoinvest company and a company called Zica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was further west. It was like maybe three kilometres away, maybe, two, two and-a-half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you that your friend Mirsad Abdurahmanovic stated that the headquarters of the military unit he belonged to was in the Zica company, would you agree with me that there were soldiers in that company?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- I am not really -- military headquarters or not. I really didn't have access there so I really cannot tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the front lines in relation to the place where the Paradiso Cafe is located were about two kilometres away; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you that the Hrasno neighbourhood had -- contains a square called Trg Heroja, or Heroes Square, would you agree with me that that was correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you that on that square there were military installations of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- there was some military headquarters there or some military installations, I am not really sure, because I really did not go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Ms. Mahindaratne, do you have any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Re-examined by Ms. Mahindaratne:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, you were cross-examined based on an official report that had been prepared in regard to the shooting incident you testified about?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit number 2114, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that report there is a reference to stray bullets. Did you ever say to any person after you were shot that -- did you ever use the term "stray bullets"?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never did use the term "stray bullet."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this official report has been prepared on the 12th of January, 1994. You were shot on 10th of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, the statement, this report, has been based on a statement you had made within two days after you were shot?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when you made that statement?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe on 11th, maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in hospital during this period?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you subject to surgery?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, did you ever mention that the shots would have come from the direction of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did at that time because I didn't look at the maps, and just it was a sniper so you really couldn't tell where the bullet came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you made that statement, had you visited -- had you had the opportunity to visit the location at which you were shot?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was in hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Bench as to where Grbavica is located as opposed to Hrasno Brdo from the point of -- point where you were standing at the time you were shot? Was it beyond Hrasno Brdo or before Hrasno Brdo, towards you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was located maybe east from Hrasno Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be able to demonstrate it better by looking at Exhibit number P3236 and tell the Bench where exactly where Grbavica was located from Hrasno Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit P3644, Mr. President? He will be able to demonstrate better.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: P3644. Exhibit number P3644.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you -- yes, but is that 3644, that is the big map?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have clean copies of 3644 because -- well, of course, if it is just -- if we could make it clear for the transcript, it could be shown to him, that's the blank map. If you don't ask for any markings, we could use it. If you want the witness to mark anything, then of course we would need a new copy of 3644, but if you say "I just want to show it to him to make it easier for him to indicate" --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is all we want to do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Usher, not to lose too much time, I think if you would put on the ELMO the part of the map which is approximately in the middle, under WHS-84, as it appears on the top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, don't mark anything, just show exactly where Grbavica was as opposed to Hrasno Brdo from where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the ELMO can zoom in. Even more to be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was Grbavica -- looking at this map, could you tell whether Grbavica was beyond Hrasno Brdo from where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was standing right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is Hrasno Brdo from there?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then it we be correct to say that Grbavica was beyond Hrasno Brdo?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, when the witness is pointing at Grbavica, it is where the map contains the text "Grbavica." When he was pointing at where he was standing when he was shot, it is in the area indicated on P Exhibit 3236, which is a part, a large part, of this map. And when he was indicating Hrasno Brdo, he was pointing at an area south of where he stood, on the map, where it seems to be without any buildings, approximately five centimetres south on the big map. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic, did you personally see any military activity being carried out at schools or any such institutions? Did you personally see for yourself?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that your friends, including Mr. Abdurahmanovic, which had not joined the military, you were testifying based on your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my personal knowledge, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How closely did you associate with them?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were older than me. I was like 17. They were about between 25 and 30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you associate with them very closely, to know about all their personal details?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know their personal details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You based your response that they had not joined the military on the basis that you always saw them in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I have no more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Husovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question for you - perhaps even a few more - but if you would just give me one second time. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that -- you initially said that the bullet would have come from Grbavica and later, when you had spoken to Mr. Hogan --

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that you told him, as you told us today, that the bullet came from Hrasno Brdo. You gave two reasons for that. The first one was that it would have been too far. Could you explain to us why it would have been too far for the shot to be fired from Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe bullet could not reach me at the time, maybe I wouldn't be hurt like I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And on what basis you would conclude that this was beyond the reach of a bullet like the one that hit you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just think that bullet can't fly more than two kilometre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what would be the distance between Grbavica and where you were?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two kilometres, something like that. I am not really sure in actual distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The second reason you gave is that you said the area was kept by the Serbs, and I take it that you referred to Hrasno Brdo.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Am I right in understanding you that since you assume that you were sniped at by the Serbs, that the bullet must have been Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. coming from an area that was controlled by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for you answers. Mr. Husovic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I thank you very much for coming to The Hague and answering questions of Defence of Prosecution and the Bench. It is important for us to hear the testimony of those who were at the relevant times and in the relevant places there and can give us their information. I know it was a long way for you. I wish you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No problem. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Husovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please guide us through the documents. Yes, that is what happens when the usher leaves the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2114, official report, police station Novo Sarajevo, date 12/01/1994; P2114.1 English translation; P3236, map marked by witness; P2097, medical documentation; P2097.1, English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Again, I would like to formulate an objection to this with relation to these exhibits, not only because I have never -- I haven't yet found out the material records report, I am still waiting for that. But what is troubling me here, Mr. President, is that if we keep the piece ERN 284149, we can see that the date of the examination appears on this record is 16th of January, 1994, which is quite obvious on the record, on the document, and we can see that this is a "6," not a "10" - in any case on my copy - Mr. President, and it is perfectly obvious. However, the translation of this document gives us a date which, as it happens, comes within the time of the incident, although the copy in Serbian, what I can see on my document, which is a date six days after the fact that we are talking about. Now, this document would give the date for the examination on the 16th and, again, we find ourselves confronted to the problem of the date. It seems again that this is Pandora's box again and this is not the box of the Defence but of the Prosecution, and we have this situation coming up on many occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne,

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Well at, this stage, Mr. President, I would not be able to explain how this discrepancy has transpired. I may have to go back to the translation branch and find out exactly how this happened. It may be that there had been another document of the same -- discharge report, letter of discharge, with this particular date. So if I may be permitted time, I could respond to this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be necessary to go to the translation department because on ERN ending 4189, Mr. Piletta-Zanin identified a clear "6." If I look at the next page, which seems to be a perhaps carbon copy, or I am not quite sure, but it would need some further examination. The --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It is quite possible, Mr. President, that on the next page, that is the 10th there and not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so that is -- whether the "6" is a "6" and whether there is a translation mistake, perhaps we would need further attention before we would have to address the translation unit. But would there be any possibility to come up with a -- I don't know what the source of this document is. I also noted that there were no questions about the document in cross-examination. Would it be possible to get closer to the source of this document so that we could solve this problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I think so, Mr. President. Sometimes what happens is when a document is not very clear, one could focus on particular areas and it is possible that the translator based his or her translation on that. So, may I be given a little bit of time to clarify this and get back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and may I take it that the witness will not be on the plane already if further issues arise out of this? I mean, it perhaps would not have -- would not need much time, but I see that there is some unclarity about whether it is a "6" or whether it is a "0." Perhaps during the break we might take a bit more time to have a closer look to it and if you could perhaps look at the files, whether this is a good copy or a contaminated copy or -- well, at least to inform us a bit more about what is not for certain a "6," but might be a "6," which would then not be in line with the clear "0" but without the preceding "1" on the ERN number 00284190. In general, Ms. Mahindaratne, we have had several, several, of this kind of problems, and I know that you are new at least in the courtroom at this very moment, but may I again stress that the Chamber would highly appreciate if documents are very carefully inspected before they are tendered. Let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber decided that before giving a decision on the admission of P2097, we will first wait for further information from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, the Defence believes that in order to test the credibility of the witness, it would be in the interest of the Defence, would be to tender the statement of Mr. Husovic that he identified as his own that he gave, and the Defence has sufficient number of copies. I believe that my colleagues have a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic, but we have indicated before that if one of the parties was intending to tender a document, that it had then to be distributed because the Chamber is not now in a position to ask any question in relation to that document because they haven't seen it. So this is not -- I mean, there might have been no objection whatsoever against admitting into evidence, but the Chamber is not now in a position to look at the document to see whether there were any additional questions necessary and you just wrote -- you just read the part that you found relevant. This is not the way to do it. I don't know whether you insist on tendering it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence insists that this exhibit should be tendered. I wanted to tender them. I had prepared them. That was my omission. When the witness identified his statement, I was only cross-examining him, and I know that you were not in a position to have the statement before you. But the point is that he claims that he was fired at from the direction of Grbavica and I believe that the Chamber did hear the witness on this issue. So I think that it would be very useful to have that within the -- within this report that the witness identified, his statement should also be included because he identified it as having been taken from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the witness has clearly testified that he gave his statement to the effect that the shots came from Grbavica, and that it was on the basis of his information that the report also states that it is Grbavica. So I don't know what the document adds to that. I mean, there is no -- as far as I can see at this very moment, the testimony is clear that it is his statement. So I don't know what the statement would add apart from that clear issue. On the other hand, let me just first hear whether Ms. Mahindaratne would have any -- would have any objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would object. If at all, the statement should have been put to the witness while he was here, and now that the witness has gone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The relevant part has been read out to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Just one -- a few words, Mr. President, and in fact given the statement came forward when I pointed out that -- in fact, the Defence counsel was pointing out a part of the official report. I have to point out that the statement was completely separate from the official report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then the statement was shown to him. He was asked whether this was the statement he gave, and the relevant portion was read out to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my submission would be there is so much more in the statement, and if the document is to be admitted, it should be have been done through the witness. In any event, the relevant portion, it has gone down in evidence. It is already there. The witness admitted that he said that the shots came from Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. The Defence will not insist on having this document tendered considering what the witness testified to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. That means that we do not give a decision yet on P2097 and P2097.1. And are there any objections against the other documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I will make my remarks later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means that 2114.1, that's P3236, are admitted into evidence. And I think that is all for the -- or did I forget one? All other documents are admitted into evidence as far as they are tendered. Would the Prosecution be ready to call its next witness or would you like to use the remaining time until the break for other reasons?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it is convenient, I could respond to the two issues that were raised earlier this morning in the remaining ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you could do that briefly. Please proceed. Or is there anything specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, in relation to the exhibits, please This has been now days - weeks, in fact - that the Prosecution has been telling us and it is now becoming a very long saga that the Prosecution is telling us, "You will find out soon. You will find out about the truth about the dates regarding the 'grattage' on the medical reports." And we have been asking for this information because we need them in order to be able to interrogate -- I believe there is a microphone that is on, on the Prosecution bench. We need those documents and the information in order to be able to examine the witnesses on these issues. Now, the time that we lose in this way, we will not be able to gain it back. And every time we ask for something, we are being told, "It was not me who asked," then they pass the ball on to somebody else, and I don't think this is correct. It is time now to give us the delay, the time, notice, a deadline, when are we going to be given this information regarding these records or they should not be admitted. Mr. President, we have shown a great deal of patience here and it is time that the Prosecution tells us clearly what is on and is this some kind of game, which is what the Defence believes that it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your observation, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I just noticed for this very moment that the type of document we just dealt with is not a similar one as the documents concerning the 'grattage'. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, firstly in relation to the issue that Mr. Piletta-Zanin has just raised, I informed you that enquiries were being made in Sarajevo in relation to that matter by an investigator, and as soon as we have the fruits of those enquiries, we will immediately inform the Trial Chamber. In relation to 92 -- the 92 bis issue, all this time we have been waiting for the translations to be done by the Translation Unit of the annexures. The latest information that we have is that will be completed by early next week. I will also review, in the same way as I have reviewed the viva voce witness list, the 92 bis witness list to see if some further deletions can be made from that list. Mr. President, in relation to the viva voce list, I have some comments to make. When I handed up that list on the 8th of May, I anticipated that we may be seeking leave to add an additional fresh witness, and that was beyond Barry Hogan, who was named on that list. It will now be apparent, of course, that that additional witness is the witness who is identified as Witness AD and whose inclusion is presently under consideration by you. On the 10th of May, I advised the Defence in a letter that was copied to the Trial Chamber that Zdenko Eterovic's name had been inadvertently been left off the list and, indeed, he is to be called today. Mr. President, there are two further witnesses who I wish to place back into our list. In other words, these are not fresh witnesses, rather, witnesses whose names have always been on the witness list but were not on that handed up by me on the 8th of May. [redacted] [redacted]. There are five witnesses who I will take off the list. They are Ismet Ceric, Viktor Andreev, Piers Tucker, Anthony Banbery and Witness V. I will provide a formal letter to the Defence and to the Trial Chamber setting out all of these details. Mr. President, that means that overall, the witness list is reduced from that which I handed up on the 8th of May. In relation to Barry Hogan, the nature of his evidence will primarily be as to what efforts have been made by the Prosecution to locate certain documents which one might otherwise have reasonably expected to be in the United Nations' archives, such as investigations carried out by UNPROFOR and various other documents. I think it appropriate that the Trial Chamber have evidence as to what steps have been taken. There will be some other matters that one might perhaps call housekeeping that will be dealt with in his statement in relation to various scheduled incidents, measurements, that sort of thing, most, if not all, of which the Defence already has in the form of incident reports in respect of each incident. It seems to me, Mr. President, that his evidence would comfortably come within 92 bis and I will make the formal application to add his name together with a 92 bis statement. I anticipate that will be next week. I don't anticipate there would be any great controversy about his evidence. Mr. President, in relation to Zoran Lecic, his name has always been on the witness list. You might recall that he has already given some evidence and I made clear at that stage that he would be recalled. There have been a number of photographs tendered, especially in relation to scheduled sniping incidents, which appear to be photographs taken from the area approximately of the suspected source of fire. He will give formal evidence about the date and position on which those photographs were taken. I anticipate he will say that he took those various photographs. He will also give some evidence about the date that the various video clips used in the opening montage came into the possession of the OTP and, indeed, his possession and therefore that would be relevant in terms of the date on which those various video clips were taken. He will also give some evidence as to the opening photographs, the photographs used in the opening. Again, I don't think it will be controversial evidence, but it may be just as well to call him in person rather than have very large photographs tendered -- attached to his statement. Mr. President, that is the present situation in relation to the witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask you one question, was Mr. Ambrosi on the witness list before us?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I dropped him. Yes, that is right, that is another deletion. I am sorry, I stand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but on the 21st of May, 2002, I see that his name is on the list for the 27th of May until the 31st of May and until the 3rd of June. So it is a bit confusing what you are telling us now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: His name has now been dropped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: His name has now been dropped. Thank you for your information. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with regard for the people here and around the courtroom, it will be better perhaps to respond to what the Prosecution had to say after the break, but I am in your hands. I will respect your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the Chamber will take the opportunity to see to what extent a response is needed to what the Prosecution has just said and that you will be given an opportunity and to what extent you will be given an opportunity to that, after the break. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before my learned colleague responds, might I raise one other issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that he will be able to respond to that as well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, on the 17th of May, the Prosecution filed a report by Richard Philips. It was filed pursuant to Rule 94 bis. The report has attached to it a number of charts. Essentially, the report depicts the structure of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps during the indictment period. That includes the identification of key personnel and also charts changes to the structure through the indictment period. Mr. President, attached to the statement and the charts, there is a document titled "References from chart Sarajevo Romanija Corps." That document which lists the references is 63 pages in length. There are an additional 10 or 20 pages still to come of references. In that filed document, there are, from time to time, these words which appear: "Please see letter dated 17 May, 2002, signed by Mark Ierace STA." That letter essentially informed the Defence and the Registry that there were further references to come. I anticipate those references will be provide in the next few days. I raise the report for this reason: That, if the Prosecution was to provide copies of the relevant passages in those documents, then those copies would number several binders, several of the thick arched lever binders. It would be an enormous task to provide that material in hard-copy form. All of the material has been disclosed to the Defence, in other words, the Defence has the material in its possession. Indeed, much of the material has come from the Defence pursuant to its obligations under reciprocal disclosure. That material, typically, is archival material by its nature from the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. Mr. President, essentially, I have a question. The question is whether the Trial Chamber requires that hard copies of the relevant excerpts be provided, in other words, be tendered as part of the report. It seems to me that the first question in responding to that really is one for the Defence, that is, whether they dispute any of his evidence as to the structure and other aspects, some aspects of the structure, such as the identification of personnel. But perhaps I could leave that with the Trial Chamber and in due course if you could let us know, we would then -- if it is -- the response is that the material is required, then we could undertake that considerable project of preparing it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you would like to respond to the observations of Mr. Ierace, you will have an opportunity to do so until a quarter past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you very much indeed, and I believe we will first answer on the matter of the testimonies. And as you can see, we did not have time to confer. We will respond at a later date on the other matter. Now, as far as the testimonies are concerned, Mr. President, we believe that we find ourselves in a very surrealist situation. For the first time in the history of his Trial Chamber, you have been given a witness statement who has self-examined and the statement went to prove what the Prosecution wants but he was never put on the witness list, on the Prosecution witness list. The least of the things would have been to say that this person, this investigator - I am not talking about Barry Hogan, I am talking about another person - at least could have been put on the witness case, which was not the case. This is the first observation I have. The second remark is that to quote in the witness's name any other person that comes from the team of the Prosecutor is not admissible. People who were investigators, that is, representatives of the Prosecution, are coming to witness for the Prosecution and this is absurd legally. I cannot understand how this can be asked for. Certainly, there was an exception to hear Mr. Lesic. But Mr. Lesic is not an investigator - I believe that is his name - he is a technician. And he was there to answer simple technical questions, that is the way the circular photographs were made, but nothing else. But I don't think it is admissible that other people should come to speak for this technician. That would not be admissible. Another point if we are constantly -- now, the Defence is trying very hard to shorten the time that is given to the Prosecution -- that is, the Defence is trying to go as fast as we can, but constantly the Prosecution is adding new witnesses Mr. President, and this is not normal. Moreover, we are told that we will get a letter explaining all this so that we will be able to prepare, a letter that we will receive in an hour or two, but that has not yet been given to us. Therefore, Mr. President, as far as new witnesses are concerned, unfortunately, the Defence's position is very firm, and that is "no." And no also because at the moment we don't have this answer to the question that has been not given to your Chamber or to us, because we have asked before your Chamber to be authorised - that was yesterday - 22 of May, in application of Rule 73(B) as it stands -- as of 8th of May, 2002. What would be wise is to first find out what will be as to your decision on the possibility or not to go ahead with the appeal and then examine the question of new witnesses. If we go the other way around, we will have this mechanics which will not work. It will complicate the matters, increase the confusion and certainly delay the proceedings. Now, considering other points that were made by Mr. Ierace, I think that we cannot immediately bring a response. We conferred, and as soon as we can do it, which is after next break, we will bring you here what our position on these other matters is. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. The Chamber has conferred during the break, Mr. Ierace, in respect of what is by now called the grattage issue. If the Prosecution would not be in a position to give the results of the investigations that are on their way at this moment, the Chamber would like to be informed within one week from now in a more detailed fashion about the efforts taken by the Prosecution in order to resolve that issue, specifically, who and especially when did what. I mean, whether there were any letters that was sent or someone sent or interviews that have taken place or that it took a couple of days to find someone who was working at that very time at that hospital, well, we would like to be informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have some news about that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We prefer to have that, even if it would be briefly in writing, so that we have a survey. If you could give us the main lines in one minute, we would be glad to hear. If not, then we just rely on any written.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I spoke to Mr. Stamp during the break. He spoke to the investigator in Sarajevo yesterday. And he will be in the Trial Chamber taking the next witness, and at the outset, he will update you on what the investigator had to say. So that investigative phase is now completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so we will hear what Mr. Stamp tells us and if it would not be satisfactory at this very moment for the Chamber, then of course still we would like to be informed within one week in more detail about the efforts made. Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Would the Prosecution be ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before that occurs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- some enquiries have also been made about the document issue which rose --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before the break. Yes, that is P2097. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps this would be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if we can deal with that. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We have the original here of which the translations and the photocopies were made. And it is pertinent to note that in the original the date seems to resemble more 10th of January, 1994, where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you want to make any further observations and, otherwise, I would like you first to hand out the original of the document to the Defence and then to the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to have another response from our learned colleague since we started these matters. Yesterday, we submitted a request to the Prosecution regarding the 1st Corps of the BH army, the material that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, we are trying not to mix up things. At this very moment, you have been given a --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...and then we will see whether at a later stage we can deal with the issue you want to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Indeed, it seems that things look different. I am not saying they are clearer; I am saying they are different. We do not see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, before commenting on the copy you just received, could you please first give it to the usher so that the Chamber can have a look at it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I apologise, Mr. President. I completely forgot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Do you need to have it back or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you very much. No. But the only thing that I wanted to say, Mr. President, is that things seem more legible, although they are not really clearer. Because if we take the translation that you received earlier, it is possible to see very well that the size of the "0" which is mentioned as a date of admission, the 10th of January, is as big as. So the "0," in its body of "0" is in the same size as the others. But when we look at the original, or at least the best copy that you have before you, we can see that the body or the size of the "0" is smaller than any other numbers, as if -- I am saying "as if" it is the lower part of another number which could have been an 8 or a 6. If we compare the previous document submitted by the Prosecution -- I am not an expert in these matters and of course it is up to you to decide on it, Mr. President. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber decides that document 2097 and 2097.1 are admitted into evidence. We did not neglect your last observation, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but as we have seen at quite some occasions before, not always a "0" is used but very often an "O" is used, at least a small type, and therefore it does not raise such doubts as not to admit the document into evidence. May I return -- Mr. Usher, could you please return this document to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: For the transcript, maybe we should say we are talking about an "O" and not a zero, and maybe we should clarify it in some way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we now see not always a "0" is used and very often a capital "O" is used. First time I said "zero," z-e-r-o, and the second time I referred to a small "o." Yes, now it is perfect. Is the -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I heard your decision and I thank you for it, but in order to facilitate the progress of justice, as this is our aim, perhaps the Prosecution could be asked to produce, if they are able to, the original of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there is a request from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can only give the answer that I have given on other occasions, which is that we did our best to obtain original documents. We have given explanations as to what steps we took, including the undertaking of a specific mission to Sarajevo following the first time that the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just cut it short? You say: "We are not in a position at that moment to provide an original."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the Chamber feels that it is not appropriate at this moment to given an order in that effect. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next witness will be taken by Mr. Stamp, who is waiting outside the court. Would you excuse Prashanthe Mahindaratne and myself, and Mr. Stamp will enter the courtroom and if you wish, he can give that explanation that I foreshadowed earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am still waiting on Mr. Stamp. I anticipate he will be here very shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the witness already waiting outside or -- ?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We then perhaps could escort the witness into the courtroom so that he can give his solemn declaration that we don't have to wait for.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will let the usher know, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Well, I see problems are, as sometimes happened, are solved. Good morning, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before calling your next witness, would you be in a position to very briefly explain to the Bench and, of course, that is an explanation for the Defence as well, what progress is made in respect of the investigation of what by now is called the "grattage."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The investigators were asked to take the documents or a sample of the documents where those grattage were clearly apparent. And they personal signed -- Dr. Debraca was asked about it. He checked his records, and I think Your Honours will recall that there is some evidence from the witness Edin Sulic took handwritten notes at the time when he did the autopsies. And he said from his records - and I am not sure if those were the notes - but from the record that he has, he confirmed that the date on the documents are correct. He says that the corrections were made at some time, but it was in 1995, and he can't remember who typed it, he can't remember when the corrections were made. He can only confirm that the dates there, which are corrections according to him, are the correct dates referring to the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that is not yet a clear explanation of what was under the correct dates and which was rubbed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, he is the only person that we could contact to begin looking into it. And he says that there are a variety of typists who pass through the place over a period of time. He would never be able to remember exactly who typed it or what was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but I think, for example, as far as my recollection goes, an allusion has been made once on the use of forms so that would explain in a more general way what might have been underneath the final correct date. But something of that kind could not be an explanation that general sense, could not be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, my Lord. A letter was sent to me in respect of the results of the enquiries and I did call the investigators and made detailed enquiries, and the doctor says he just can't recall who corrected it and at what stage. He knows that he signed them and he knows that the dates, as he sees them there, are the correct dates from his records, and the names that he sees are the names of the persons on whom he conducted autopsies. But given time as he was given by the investigators in Sarajevo, he was not able to remember the details of anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of how it happened. Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, considering that this was a very swift explanation by Mr. Stamp, the French booth was not able to hear the names of the doctor and of another person. Could you, Mr. Stamp, please repeat the names of a doctor and of another person.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises, I didn't catch Mr. Piletta-Zanin's --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if there is a problem of interpretation. Do you want me to speak in English? [In English] The names you just gave me a moment ago, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The name is Dr. Debraca, which is the same name which appears on the documents. I am trying to recall who is the other person I referred to by name. I don't think I referred to any other person by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't doubt your memory, but I think you may have mentioned a patient or documents in relation to other patients, but that doesn't matter. Mr. President, am I authorised to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
